How the latency probes measure the loop

Where each instant is stamped, on whose clock, and which subtraction gives which number. Both probes light a lamp, wait for the host to see it in a frame, and time the answer coming back.

From tasks/Latency/LatencyProbe.py, tasks/Latency/InferenceProbe.py and source/video/latency_probe.py

microcontroller, its own clock photons and the camera host, its own clock the timed instants

The LED probe: photons to a state machine that can act

The inference probe: the same loop, with the tracker inside it

Which subtraction gives which number

QuantityClockSubtractionWhat it is
CAPTUREMCUt_capture − t_on Exposure, transport and decode. Quantised by one frame period.
RESTMCUt_ack − t_capture Detection and the serial return.
TOTALMCUt_ack − t_on Photons to a state machine that can act on them. The number a live experiment lives with.
T_hosthostpush_queued − capture What the host itself spent, from the probe log.
T_returnhostping→pong / 2 One serial leg, measured rather than assumed.
T_cameraderivedTOTAL − T_host − T_return Photons to cap.read() returning. No host instrumentation can reach this directly.

Only the last line crosses clocks, and it subtracts durations rather than instants, so no offset between the two clocks enters. It assumes only that they tick at the same rate: 50 ppm of crystal mismatch is 15 ms across a five-minute run but under 0.02 ms within one trial, far below the 1 ms floor.

What the lamps are for

LampFired byMarks
GREEN, LED-Athe board, at t_on The stimulus. This is the one the host hunts for and detects.
BLUEthe board, at t_capture Marks the frame that carried the flash. A visual check only.
RED, LED-Bthe board, after t_ack The answer came back. Lit after the stamp, so it is outside the measurement.

Both lamps are proven before anything is timed: RED blinks 3 times, then GREEN 10 times. Without that opening you cannot tell a dead answer lamp from a loop that never closes — both look like "only one LED is blinking", and that ambiguity has already cost rig sessions.

Inference, 2 cameras at 30 fps33 ms 114 / 113 ms62 / 611077 / 1061
Inference, 1 camera at 98 fps10 ms 66 ms411122

The frame period dominates the loop. Tripling the rate roughly halves the round trip, on both probes. Subtracting the two at 30 fps gives about 40 ms as what SLEAP inference costs the loop; at 99 fps it is about 32 ms, which is the model's own time rather than the camera's.
